title: Machine learning-guided design and synthesis of benzimidazole-based HDAC inhibitors: prospective validation of a fine-tuned pretrained graph transformer
content: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are established targets in cancer therapy, yet the prospective discovery of potent inhibitors remains challenging. Here we combined task-specific fine-tuning of the pretrained graph transformer GROVER with ensemble screening, synthesis and biological validation. With the classifier held fixed, fine-tuning increased GROVER's test-set accuracy from 86.07% to 92.54% and its ROC-AUC from 94.65% to 96.16% with Random Forest, and by a similar margin with XGBoost and a multilayer perceptron. Fine-tuned GROVER gave the highest accuracy of the eighteen combinations tested, 93.53%, whereas ECFP4 with Random Forest gave the highest ROC-AUC, 96.55%. The three classifiers were then used as an ensemble to screen sixty synthetically accessible compounds across ten derivative series. Series IX, six benzimidazole-based (E)-cinnamohydroxamic acids differing in their aryl cap and its ring position, was the only series in which every member was predicted active, and all six were synthesised and evaluated. Every compound inhibited HDAC in HeLa nuclear extract, three more potently than vorinostat and two comparably. IXf, which carries the 4-fluorophenyl cap at the benzimidazole 6-position, reached enzymatic and cellular half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of 19.33 and 57.05 nM, with approximately 4-fold greater enzymatic potency than vorinostat. It was also more antiproliferative than vorinostat in HeLa and SK-BR-3 cells and induced G2/M-phase arrest and apoptosis. All six showed more favourable calculated ligand–HDAC2 interaction energies than vorinostat, five of them improving at the pocket rim. These findings demonstrate that task-specific fine-tuning of pretrained graph representations can support the discovery of experimentally validated HDAC inhibitors.
